review:
First of all, a couple things about my playthrough:

- Solo, with some tweaks to the server settings to make it less grindy (boosted gather rate, refinement rate, things like that).
- Reached Dunley Farmlands / Iron Gear so far.
- Dipped my toe into multiplayer, didn't bother with the official servers.

[i][b]The Positives[/b][/i]:
[list]
[*] Great gothic art style.
[*] PvE Combat is fun and challenging, especially with large groups of mobs.
[*] Weapon fighting styles feel unique and lend themselves to different tactics.
[*] Spells are fairly diverse.
[*] Interior decorating.
[*] Plethora of server setting options to customize the experience and lessen the grind for solo play, if so desired.
[*] Castle layout changes are mostly fairly easy, especially when you set the resource return rate to 100% (because I'm gonna reorganize my castle design and NO, I will NOT grind for it!). Free movement of objects in your castle is a god-send.
[*] Some bosses are thrilling, nail-biting affairs with near-misses and clutch moments abound. (Bright Archer, Bandit King)
[*] The sense of humor.
[/list]

[i][b] The Negatives [/b][/i]:
[list]
[*] Otherwise smooth framerate punctuated by relatively long (~0.5-1 sec) periods of stuttering, even on Medium settings.
[*]  Castle layout changes get very fiddly in certain situations. [strike]Can't delete stray floors if they have a wall on top of them.[/strike] As of Patch 0.5.42050, you can now delete floors even if there's a wall on top of them (with a few exceptions). There's still the lack of ease in switching the position of your Castle Heart, which I just thought of now, so I'll keep the general case in.
[*] The grid feels a bit restrictive when building gravel paths.
[*] [strike]Weirdly difficult to make a good looking garden.[/strike]
[*] Some bosses are a bit boring and too easy even for solo play. (That ice guard guy, the Shadow Priestess).
[*] Server settings cannot be changed for an existing server easily, even if the server isn't running. It is technically possible to do it, but it requires fiddling with JSON files which may be intimidating for the casual user. Not so hard when you know what's up, but takes a bit too much research for what should be an easy adjustment in-game.
[*] No apparent ability to customize servant mission lengths. Sure, I could leave my computer on overnight and plop my character in the coffin, but I really don't think that's ideal. Besides, the world's got enough computer heat output without me adding to it.
[*] Can't pause during solo play. Should be an easy enough fix, since a similar game, Valheim, did that within the first few patches.
[*] Solo servers should keep some world effects permanent [spoiler](blowing up the Bandit Stronghold gates)[/spoiler]
[/list]

Overall, well worth the twenty bucks I spent. Very fun, even if I'm not playing multiplayer, which seems to be the primary game mode they're concerned with. The negatives were mostly minor annoyances that don't detract that much from the overall experience.

Now, for a wishlist of things I'd like them to expand upon. These are mostly big things that I'd never expect them to accomplish anytime soon.

[i][b]Wishlist[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Servants. For we lonesome solo players, some help in gathering local building materials would be welcome. We also should be able to tell them to do things around the castle -- feed the prisoners if food is available, kill any ghouls that pop up out of the tombs, gather materials from refinement stations and place them in a designated chest, personally fetch us some blood from the blood cabinet, etc. What else are they there for if not to make our decadent, immortal lives easier?
[*] PvE castle sieges. The local bandits / militia / spiders should try and siege nearby castles on occasion. Should be toggleable, obviously, or limited to certain times like with PvP castle sieges.
[*] More facial feature options. The game has an excellent variety of hairstyles, but the beard selection is paltry.
[*] Separate eyebrow options from the face options, if possible.
[/list]

[b] This is a PvE review: [/b]
 
I like this game a lot, as it has many elements i personally enjoy in video games, from base building, items crafting, material farming, planning and preparing for boss fights, then unlocking new items and abilities to make yourself more powerful, and try to beat the next challenge.

[h1] What I like: [/h1]

[b] The blood mechanic - [/b] since you play as a vampire you rely on drinking the blood of your victims to keep yourself alive, however there are different types of blood that open up different types of buffs and bonuses for you. Say for example you wanna go farm for stones, why not drink a worker blood and increase the amount of raw material you yield. Obviously blood comes with different purity levels... so the higher purity you get, the more bonuses you unlock for that type of blood, so happy hunting.

[b] The spells system - [/b] as you start the game you will have access to a limited number of spells, but from the beginning you will have a glimpse at a spell book that has a lot of hidden spell slots you need to unlock, the starting spells are useful enough to get you through the early game challenges, and you can even keep using them until the end if you enjoy them, but in order to unlock new spells you have to beat certain bosses, drinking their blood will unlock their knowledge and grants you new abilities.

The game wants you to experiment with spell builds, especially when fighting specific bosses, if you find yourself struggling it wouldn't be a bad idea to try different spells.

[b] The jewels system - [/b] it's your standard gem system, where you enhance spells by equipping jewels on them, to unlock modifiers or boost the spells effects, you can find these jewels as random drops, but you will have access to crafting them later on, so you can customize and fine tune your favorite spells to your liking.

[b] Boss fights - [/b] for the most part they are very well designed, challenging but fair and satisfying to beat, I managed to solo everything with the right spells, blood types, and practice, again the fights can be very challenging (especially solo) but they can definitely be won (I mean, I managed lol), some even can feel easy if you know what you are doing and have the right tools. 

The fights are not won by thoughtless aggression, they are designed to test your reflexes for sure, but for the most part it's more about, patience, learning the boss patterns, putting a strategy for your approach and again having the right tools and buffs.

[b] Gear Score - [/b] the game has a variety of weapons, armors, and accessories to use, you start with basic stuff and unlock more advanced and powerful stuff the further you play, the total score of equipped items determines the damage output against enemies, and how much damage you receive from them.

Different weapons unlock different skills to use the more advanced the weapon is. So you can go charging with a claymore, smacking and stunning your enemy, you could use something lightweight instead and be evasive and sneaky, or you could bring firearms and start blasting.

[b] The servants - [/b] at one point in the game you will be able to convert strong warriors or hardworking farmers into vampires, granting them the gift of immortality, which they will wisely use to be at your service.. Forever...
you can equip your servants with items to increase their score level as well, and then send them into hunts that could last from 2 to 23 hours, in real time.. Once the hunt is over your servants will return with a lot of goods for you, which lower the amount of time you spend grinding for stuff.. Recently there was an update which allowed the hunts timer to keep counting even when you go offline, if you are not playing on a dedicated server, so you can now use the full potentials of your servants, if you choose to play solo offline.

[b] Blood hunts - [/b] as mentioned in the start, blood type plays an important part in this game, and the higher quality of blood you get the better bonuses you will unlock, it's rare to come by the highest quality of blood in the game, I don't want to spoil a lot, but let's say there is a way to get hold of individuals that have high quality blood, and have them as guest in your castle.. make sure you feed them well, and keep them happy so you don't lose them... after all they have high quality blood.

[b] Base building - [/b] It's good and intricate, if you enjoy base building it's satisfying enough, you need to plan where you build and place stuff, some machinery requires specific environments to work at full efficiency.

[h1] What i don't like (not much honestly): [/h1]

Some bosses require more balancing, especially when it comes to adds spawning and the risk/reward ratio.

Spell/Skill balancing sometimes suffer from the game having both PVE and PVP modes.

Not having end game cycle with more contents/activities, which is understandable since the game is still in early access.

The game got a lot of improvement when it comes to optimization in the past year, but it still needs more work, nothing unplayable, but still needs more work.

[b] For me this game is a real gem, it's worth picking up and playing if you enjoy base building, skill based challenging boss fights and a lot of cool mechanics to explore and experiment with, can be played solo offline, online PvE solo or with friends, and if you are young enough you can even try PvP :P [/b]

[i] Thank you for reading this!! and remember this is only a one man's opinion. [/i]

The central gameplay loop of V Rising is pretty interesting and satisfying: acquire resources, upgrade your gear and castle, hunt new bosses to unlock new spells, abilities, forms, and recipes, and repeat. If you're willing to tolerate a grind or want to play offline with custom settings that reduce the grind, you'll enjoy the gameplay. 

Some have likened it to Diablo or PoE. Given that it's WASD, I'm not sure I really see the comparison-- the combat is a little more technical and skillful than most ARPGs. The bosses usually require good timing and footwork and a focus on mitigating your own greed if you're properly/under-leveled. It's more like a Hades or Heroes of Hammerwatch type game minus the roguelike run-based upgrades. You have abilities on cooldown, like D2 or D3, but precision and timing matter, unlike D2, D3, or the first 90 hours of PoE. I love D2, but the difficulty is much more gear-based than skill-based. Most of my buddies are struggling with the late game bosses while gently overleveled. The first several bosses will be rather easy if you're familiar with Dark Souls type patience, but the latter bosses become genuinely interesting and require some practice and planning to take down. They're easily the best part of the game.

V Rising is entertaining, but you need to understand that a given playthrough (in online or on default server settings) is 90% grind and 10% gameplay.

The first 10 hours of a playthrough communicate this poorly: they're consistently fun. You're upgrading your gear and abilities with solid pacing, and it takes an hour or less to acquire the resources you need to upgrade that gear once you unlock the needed recipes. Each time you acquire a new ability, it's fairly likely you'll feel significantly more powerful and more able to collect the resources you like without worrying about the ads guarding them. The most frustrating grind during this stage of play is acquiring enough stone and wood to wall in your castle to maintain a decent little workshop while keeping out the sunlight. Eventually, each tier upgrade for loot is much grindier than this.

Once you're about 20 hours in, you have some of, if not THE, best abilities in the game. Bosses, at that point, essentially only guard recipes. Once you get to the second-to-last tier of weapons and armor, the resource grind slows to a halt. You have to run the most efficient routes for hours to outfit yourself, much less a team. The novelty and excitement of getting what were previously rare items totally fades by the time you finally get a tiny stat upgrade. Most of my friends lost interest here, and I was left playing the game largely solo. It's fair to say that a good number of people that would have enjoyed this game if it were setup like a roguelike became sick of the grind:boss fight ratio. When the progression still feels fun, the bosses will be a bit underwhelming. When the bosses start getting fun, the progression feels underwhelming (grind! Are you tallying how many times I've said the word yet?).

I think that grindy games are fun if you spend no more than half of your playtime grinding, and if that grinding presents varied areas, enemies, and experiences that are roughly equally viable. This isn't that. There's often 1 or 2 areas that are by far the best for acquiring your most needed resource, leading either to boring repetitiveness or acceptance of subpar farming routes in a game that demands a bunch of farming. The scourgestone/dark silver grind is really frustrating, especially because the end game forge requires the equivalent of 3 tool's/weapon's worth of it before you can actually make the tools/weapons. You'll run the Haunted Forest and Dunley Monastery a dozen times to get what you need. You'll be able to farm these areas like the back of your hand. The challenge, novelty, and intrigue will be gone.

On the business side, it seems Stunlock isn't really to be trusted as a developer, either. They've abandoned 2 different Early Access titles already, and they've added expensive "supporter" DLCs to this game without having released a major update in 10 months. This is good news in that old guides still apply if you're looking to learn the optimal routes and strategies in this game. This is bad news if you're expecting this game to become much more than it already is. At the very least, this game is already well worth $20 as it stands.

Pros:
-Satisfying combat with gradually more challenging bosses
-Good upgrade system tied to gear instead of XP (somebody else can grind for you if you don't have time and just wanna do the fun parts)
-Starts out feeling like a Souls title in combat
-Ends up making you feel incredibly powerful with proper cooldown management in combat
-New animal forms to help you navigate the map
-Castle offers more and more functionality
-Lets you run your own server with custom settings to tweak resource and combat difficulty
-Servants can farm a little for you while you're offline

Cons:
-While you do unlock new mechanics to mitigate grind, perfectly using all of them still leaves you feeling slower to acquire resources than you were in the first 10 hours
-Eventually, entire play sessions will be spent grinding. Is the combat fun enough for you to offset this?
-Unlikely to receive many major updates
-If your friends are reasonable, responsible, employed adults, they'll lose interest
-Bosses are much more fun solo than with friends even though this is a multiplayer-focused game
-Can't fast travel while carrying anything important, and you'll travel to the same areas over and over and over. Game would still be painfully grindy if you could fast travel anywhere you wanted anytime you wanted, so it adds insult to injury.
-Game promises you a bat form only to reveal you can't use it while carrying anything important, making it worse than the teleportation network available at the beginning of the game in most scenarios
-Failing to plan around the day/night cycle can result in boss/grinding attempts interrupted or postponed
-Have to log on consistently to make the most of your servants
-Ideal castle locations will be overcrowded on online. You'll have to build yours in butthole town, approximately seven years from all your ideal farming spots.

My suggestion? Pick this game up. The best moments are too entertaining to pass up what it already offers for $20. But don't play online. Play a private server with custom settings with friends or solo. Make resources twice as abundant and recipes half as expensive (Honestly? Maybe even make recipes a third or fourth as expensive). Don't touch combat difficulty (make it harder if you're on a 2nd playthrough or perfectionistic: some of these bosses are so well-designed that they're worth learning to no-hit). Enable the fast travel network to be always active, even if you're carrying "cannot be teleported" items (maybe put this one off for a second playthrough if you love the feeling of exploration). If you really must play it in its full, grindy glory, your second playthrough will always be waiting for you.
A fun game but also one that throws a lot of time sinks at you. If you don't have a lot of time to play you may want to give this one a pass.

You can play the game without any PvP at all and still have a great time, in an experience akin to Valheim.
You build your own vampire castle (with lots of cosmetic options), gaining new powers and knowledge for each boss you successfully hunt, while trying to navigate the different contested sources of resources to secure your development.

The PvE bosses are enjoyable and well designed with varied, clear and recognizable attack patterns or AoEs to dodge.
Most of them are accessible enough to be done solo while still providing a good challenge, which can encourage vampires to cooperate together.

Servers can tweak their rules to differenciate themselves from one another, allowing for a variety of different playstyles.
Boss health and damage, drop rates, being able to teleport items around or not, being able to raid bases or not, many things can change alongside max clan number.

After 150 hours, I am finally "done" with a singular run of the game. There is a lot of things to say about this game, the game has a lot of good points, but also some questionable aspects. 

[h1]The good[/h1]

[list]
[*] The game looks great! The environment design is very well done and the graphics are stunning!
[*] The base-building system is very competent, in particular, the base relocation system is awesome and something I haven't seen any other game do nearly as well
[*] The bosses are very varied mechanically and are all pretty interesting to fight (although I'm not a big fan of the fact that many of them spawn minions)
[*] The game offers visually distinct storage furniture for each category of items, I wish more games did this!
[/list]

[h1]The slightly questionable things[/h1]

[h2]The combat[/h2]
The game's combat system takes some getting used to. Your dodge option has a very long cooldown (8 seconds), while bosses attack much faster than that. The bosses are designed so that most attacks can be dodged with regular movement once you know how the bosses's moveset work, but it still makes your first fight with each boss a not very fun experience.

Furthermore, the game has a weird approach to healing - as in, healing is not really a thing. For the first half of the game, your only real healing option is "blood-mend", except it locks you in a T-pose stance while you heal, which is sub-optimal in the middle of combat. 
Starting the second half of the game, you do unlock enough skills and items to be able to make a build that can self-heal, however that remains limited, and there is in fact a hard cap on how much you may heal, and the workings of this cap are so unclear that I have still not figured out how it works after 150 hours.
- To give you an idea, essentially, if you get take a full combo to the face, most of the HP you lost is unrecoverable and you just have to not get hit again. 
I can't say I very much liked that, it made some bosses feel like a DPS race..   

[h2]The PvE[/h2]

I played on a PvE server with friends, we didn't want the pressure of PvP, and certainly didn't want the pressure of having to protect our bases from other players.
After playing for a while, it became pretty clear that the game is very much designed for PvP and that PvE was an afterthought. Some of the boss/main quest rewards have no use in PvE... 
The game also does not let you teleport if you have "valuable" (which is a lot of items) items in your inventory, presumably so that other players can attack you and take it from you when you're on your way home, but in PvE that just feels like an annoying, arbitrary restriction. 

Another thing that is leans heavily towards PvP and has little purpose in PvE is the "Soul Shards", those are end-game equipment that drop from the last 4 bosses of the game, geared specifically for PvP (+15% damage to vampires, so other players). These can only be stored in their own specific (huge!) storage furniture, which appears on the map of other players (for base raiding purposes,  so completely irrelevant in PvE) and they lose durability simply by existing. After having lost all their durability (within a day or two), you can only repair them by killing the bosses of incursions, a world map invasion event (which itself isn't very fun because very repetitive). 
Obtaining those soul shards on a PvE server left us wondering "what the hell do we do with those...?" 

[h2]The grind curve[/h2]

The grind curve gets pretty rough, it took me ~150 hours to "complete" (kill the final boss). You progress at a good pace until mid-game where the curve starts becoming a straight vertical line. It was rough enough that for a few weeks I was mostly just letting my servants do passive farming for me until I had enough resources to craft the equipment I needed to progress. 
So you know what you're getting into, according to the Steam achievements, only 5.2% of players have beaten the final boss, which may suggest that a lot of players have dropped the game before finishing it (maybe also because of the final boss being a huge difficulty spike)

[h2]Yeah the final boss is something alright[/h2]

I'm not actually sure how I feel about it, but yeah as I stated before, the final boss is a massive difficulty spike - intentionally so, the boss was given multiple different opening voice lines amongst other things because the developers very much expect you to get shit on the handful first few times you fight him. 
I don't know what horror this boss must be on "brutal" difficulty and frankly I don't want to find out :), but I do have a lot of respect for the 1.2% of players who did beat it on brutal 

[h1]Where cosmetics :([/h1]
This is a very minor thing all things considered, but I am a bit disappointed in the lack of cosmetic outfits. There is a cosmetic system which sees practically no use in the base game, it does see a bit more use with DLCs but still not so much, which feels like a bit of shame considering that the framework is there.

[h1]The very questionable[/h1]

[list]
[*] The game does NOT let you pick a specific amount out of a stack of items. The game only lets you split a stack of items in half, which is incredibly frustrating.
[*] Compounding with the above missing basic QoL feature, crafting tables are not able to take materials from nearby storage, forcing you to move around your castle a lot when crafting. This is pretty baffling as the game asks you to make specific rooms for each "type" of crafting (so you'll have a forge room, an alchemy room...) so it would be intuitive for the crafting tables to be able to take materials from storage that is in the same room. 
[*] Because of the above, crafting and storing resources felt like a genuine chore and takes much longer than it should :(
[*] I talked about how the game has distinct storage for each category of items earlier and how that was great - but it's not perfect. Some items are categorized very awkwardly; For instance, Power Cores are categorized as an "alchemy" item, so you put it in either alchemy storage of generic storage, but power cores do not have a single recipe in alchemy, they're only used in forging and jewelry, so they're very unintuitive to store..
[*] The building system is overall very competent - except for stairs. The game does not let you replace staircases even if it's the same type of staircase with only a different skin, and that is despite having a feature that lets you easily change the color of furniture with multiple color options. The game does not let you remove stairs either if they're the only stairs connecting to the upper floor, so if you want to be able to change your stairs when you unlock new stairs, you NEED to build two sets of stairs for all your castle floors..
[*] Trading with humans is practically worthless, despite it being a hassle to do in the first place. Human traders rarely have the items you're looking for, particularly when it comes to seeds, seeds are incomprehensibly hard to get...
[*] Some of the animal forms have very little use. Rat form is useful for sneaking around, wolf form helps you get around faster, bear form lets you mine big deposits of minerals, bat form lets you fly, and... spider form lets you... dig into the ground (???) to "hide from enemies and the sun", except you can't move at all and enemies can still hit you anyway?? and toad form lets you jump higher but there is seemingly no benefit from being able to do so?
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

The fact that the "good" section is a lot smaller than the rest of the review may be misleading, I'm nitpicking a lot, the game is overall very good, although I really don't get why would anyone play PvP? I also don't see this game being nearly as fun without friends.
As for the replayability, ehhhh... I definitely don't feel like replaying even with the upcoming expansion, the game's progression is very linear

In official PvE servers players are able to entirely block off sections of the map from being accessible with their castles. If I was feeling petty or just being thoughtless, I could surround someone's castle and never let them leave, and there's not a thing the devs have done to stop this. From what I saw when I looked it up, their response is that it's 'legal'.

In my case my late game castle is now entirely inaccessible along with everything my friends and I have worked to collect and create. I can't teleport any of the items that are there out, so it's all useless, and I can't bring any new items in. I can't even break it all down and move it. There's no recourse, and that's the kind of frustration that makes me leave my first negative review ever. It's the kind of experience where I'm forced to quit not because I don't want to play but because I can't play any more. 

Should the devs fix this, I think the game's a blast. Perhaps some sort of 'you can't put a foundation here, as this would block all paths to X area' system in PvE servers?

It has one map but it's carefully crafted, progression takes you from one zone to another while each zone is distinct and well-defined, has its mood, and is set up with a nice attention to detail and nice mob variety. 

Now if you're interested in the PVP in short don't, spare yourself. Whereas the PVP is one of the most fun PVPs you might have it's unfortunately poorly balanced. PVP servers usually last 2 weeks before dying and you have to repeat the progression to enjoy another 2 weeks, Meta builds tend to be spammed in the open world and render the game very stale and boring, raiding mechanics haven't been optimized since forever, and feels like they gave up on them among other things. 

This game isn't a live service game it's an indie game and the devs said that they don't have plans or intention for players to keep playing this game forever, so it ends, your "endgame" will either be PVP or decorating and because it's not constantly balanced for PVP or quite frankly, they don't know how to, that's why all these issues exist, side note Vrising is from the same devs of battlerite, you can see how that one ended up. 

With all that being said Vrising till the time of this review remains maybe the only Melee and magic open-world PVP game outside of MMORPGs and it's still more unique since it has a targeting system that makes it skill-reliant 

All in all it's a great game and it goes on cheap, also all the DLCs are cosmetics, you just need the base game and you have access to all the contents.

Let me preface this review by saying that [i]I really want to like this game[/i]. It has a lot of potential and is an interesting blend of well established genres that seem to work together rather well. Rather than bore you with an essay that is miles long let me list my current gripes with the game and suggest some things that, if changed could change my opinion.

[h2]Positives:[/h2]
- combat is skill based and fun to experiment with
- world seems interesting and lore keeps me engaged
- wide variety of spells, abilities to choose from leading to experimentation with builds
- boss designs are fun, challenges arise in PVE though, more on that later.
- Castle building is fun and gives a sense of progression

[h2]Negatives:[/h2]
- certain combat skills are much better than others, wasting the potential in variety
- upgrade path is extremely linear, there  is exactly 1 type of armor per tier
- servant mission timers are based on 'real time' meaning you need to wait a whopping 24 hours for a full, well prepared mission to complete, seeing as to how many resources you need late game this makes grinding a chore and not fun.
- late game bosses are damage sponges, difficulty curve is widely inconsistent make certain later bosses feel easier than earlier ones.
- locking gear progression behind bosses and making player power scale directly with said gear, can make for a frustrating experience in PVE leaving the player with no choice but finding that exact combination of skills + chugging potions to beat a boss.
- No reason to keep playing after final boss has been defeated, no replayability in PVE
- Bear and Toad form serve exactly 1 purpose and 1 purpose only, switching between them is slow resulting in what is thematically a cool concept into a skill that I avoid using.

[h2]Suggested Fixes:[/h2]
- introduce gear variety (3 per tier) to give greater player flexibility. Tanky gear that gives more defense buffs at the cost of speed, mage gear to boost casting, rogue gear to boost nimble DPS. This should also help with enhancing the viability of certain skills.

- Gear enchantments or gem socketing for gear makes the gem station more useful, also again this can result in similar benefits as above

- Merge some of the animal forms to make them more usable and interesting, keep the boss fight unlocks but power up 1 or 2 of these forms whenever you do instead of 1 trick pony forms.

- Add a randomly generated dungeon system for late game that is accessed through waygates (in the vein of Path of Exile) this could greatly increase player retention

This is a wonderful vampire fantasy adventure and base building and crafting game. There is an impressive game map, oodles of enemies and items, and lots of fun thematic elements. The music is pretty nice too. The overall soundboard is great, and there are fun voice lines for all the enemies. The game world feels alive in a way, and it's pretty immersive for a top-down game. The graphics and visuals are a somewhat unique cartoonish style that I find both lighthearted and grim at the same time. There is a day-night cycle, critical to a vampire's concerns for obvious reasons, in which you find yourself managing activities based on time. The base building is fun and role immersive, meaning you can make your castle spooky and strange, utilitarian, silly, or whatever suits you. For PvP, it's obviously more about defensive and offensive strategy. 

As a small disclaimer, I enjoy this game casually, having spun up my own PvE server. I've not taken part in PvP. I hear it gets pretty intense, I just frankly don't enjoy PvP in this sort of game. I've never played on public servers!

PvE is often challenging, especially all the mini-bosses you must defeat to earn various powers and crafting recipes. Combat in general is fun because it does require some effort, with each enemy type and each boss having their own mechanics to learn and play around. There are many different weapons and spells, each with their own unique abilities, flavor, and preferred enemy effectiveness. I find I have one main setup that I usually enjoy, switching to different weapons or even changing spells on occasion if a particular enemy is difficult or calls for a wildly different strategy.

There are a huge number of recipes and crafted items. As you go along, you unlock more. These items range from base parts, crafting stations, storage boxes, weapons, armor, potions, and the list goes on. All of the things are interesting and unique, and you find yourself excited to craft the next new thing.

I really enjoy all the transforming abilities. It's pretty fun being able to turn into a bat, bear, wolf, toad, rat, or even don a 'human disguise' for trading coin for goods with the locals. The various forms unlock the ability to traverse the landscape in new ways, or even aid in combat. I also enjoy the horse riding method of getting around the map, especially once you can 'dominate' a horse to make it into your own special spooky vampire horse hoopty.

There's also an interesting facet of play involving the magical capture of NPC's. They can be taken as servants and sent on supply missions or even used to defend your base from PvP attacks. You can also capture and keep various NPCs you find in game, imprisoning them. You must feed them and balance their health and misery gauges to keep them alive. You do this because they can supply your character with blood of various types depending on whom you've imprisoned,  each NPC type is also blood type and will have a random quality percentage. These can weakened in combat and then fed upon in the field, killing them, to receive temporary relevant bonuses to your character. However, capturing them means you can choose to have an ongoing supply of a desirable bonus. While adventuring, simply identify an NPC with a blood type conferring the desired bonuses that is of high quality. You weaken them, then "dominate" them magically to lead them to your prison. It's a pretty interesting system in my opinion.

You will eventually have legendary items and armors which confer various bonuses, as well as modifier items to 'tweak' spells in various ways. Through these, you can create custom "builds" to play in a way that suits you. There are so many that I couldn't begin to guess how many possibilities there are. I love that level of deep customization in any game, though at first it's a bit overwhelming perhaps. I started just using whatever I found until I got a few items which seemed to play well together or combo in fun ways.

As far as end game, well that remains to be seen for me. I've got 139 hours in at the time of this review. I've build a few different bases across two character runs. I'm currently only about 3/4 of the way through the bosses I think. I do believe there are some extra hard challenge bosses at the end. I think the only real end-game beyond that is just playing around with base building, perfecting character builds, collecting the cosmetic helmets, or perhaps moving onto trying PvP- but from what I understand that really requires a team of friends to accomplish successfully and have fun doing so. There probably are solo/no-teaming servers for PvP, but as I mentioned I'm not personally interested in PvP in this sort of game.

There are a couple cosmetic dlc's you can purchase. These in no way at all enhance character power or ability, nor are they required in the least to play and enjoy every item and area of the game. This is a huge plus to me, as so many other games have gone a bad direction with dlc's.

Negatives?

Well, it can be a bit boorish alone if you aren't into this sort of base-building/crafting/harvesting game. Best to play with a few friends, as is often the case for many games. Controls are a bit hard to master at first, with mouse cursor position dictating attack direction independent of WASD, all while using right mouse button to rotate the camera around. And it can be a bit hard for some- I wouldn't let the cartoonish graphics fool you, this game can be brutal. Steering the horse was a pain at first too, but eventually you'll get the hang of it. (not sure if there's controller support or not, I use keyboard/mouse) And lastly, I feel that while the character creation options are mostly sufficient, the armor 'looks' cannot be changed. This bothers me. You can customize the character, and collect dozens of different capes and hats, but you cannot currently change your armor appearance or color. The armor just is what it is. Not that it looks bad, but I really feel they missed the bar by not creating a customization option for the armor colors. It's not a deal breaker, but it does bug me. A role-playing game of any sort in 2023 should have all kinds of character customization! Maybe they'll add that in the future? Let's hope. ** EDIT** 2024 now, and there is customization for outfits, and they've added Castlevania items and boss! AMAZING!

I hope you enjoyed my review! It's not very in depth, but I feel you can watch gameplay on youtube to get a better sense of the visuals, combat, and crafting. I do highly recommend this game overall, and especially so if you enjoyed Valheim, 7-days, Ark, or other base builders.

There should be a "It Depends" option for whether or not I'd recommend this game. For those of you who find fulfillment in beating nine kinds of hell out of each other, I'm not in a position to speak for you. 

I prefer to play single player. If you do too, this game is probably not for you, and isn't being designed for you.

Don't get me wrong, it's got a lot to recommend it; interesting mechanics, decent combat, cool artwork, elaborate setting, promising but limited castle building... but ultimately, nothing that fulfills the RPG enthusiast, at least not at this stage of its development. You get the hint of a vast backstory, but never more than a hint. You get some interesting bosses, but no real connection between them and you, and no storyline to compel you to pursue them other than that they're next in line. 

I actually put hundreds of hours into the game, though given some of the server mechanics, it's hard to tell how many of those hours were spent playing, and how many were just leaving my game up overnight to accomplish real time processes. That isn't a complaint, just an explanation of "time spent." 

But I did play through to the last boss, and had to adjust server setting (and restart from the beginning) to get that far, since combat is designed around multi-player. And once done, I ended up looking back and thinking "why did i spend so much time on this game?"

That may sound contradictory, but what I mean is, while the mechanics can be compelling, and keep you moving forward, looking for more, ultimately you never find it. You have a lot of combat. You craft a lot of stuff, you do a lot of building, you meet a lot of seemingly interesting characters. But you never get a reason why you did all that. 

So if you prefer playing single-player games that offer a fulfilling single-player experience, this is not it, and isn't intended to be it.

I found V Rising to be a surprisingly good game. Why surprising? Well, I wasn't expecting much. I never heard of Stunlock Studios before, and only bought it because it was going cheap and a friend recommended it (for the base building).

The graphics are the first thing that struck me. They're pretty simple, but the style the devs used is very effective and the result looks stunning. The appearance of this game will age well.

The combat is a lot of fun. There's a large variety of weapons, and they all perform differently, and have their own special moves/attacks. Initially this can be overwhelming, but as you learn what each weapon does then it becomes obvious that the range and versatility means you can take many approaches to combat. There's something for everyone here. Combat is expanded by the huge number of spells which also have many different effects. Both weapons and spells can be modified and tailored to your liking. Several sets of armour are available at each tier, catering for various styles of play (tank, mobility, magic), along with a range of buffs (via potions, elixirs, and "blood types"). It's a comprehensive and well balanced system.

When it comes to fighting bosses and combat in general, some of the bosses and packs of mobs roam around. This can be used to your advantage if you engineer a situation where you kite a boss into a bad situation, but sometimes you might get ambushed by mobs or even another boss. Personally I found this highly entertaining, and spent hours stalking bosses who might otherwise be too difficult, waiting for a scenario that could swing the battle my way. If fighting where you may be interrupted then it pays to be aware of your surroundings.

Base building is straightforward yet impressive. You can build a massive castle without much effort, and the range of devices and decorations is vast. If you enjoy pottering around with bases then there's a lot to keep you occupied, but if you just want something quick and easy then the V Rising provides that too.

The game loop revolves around killing (about 65) bosses to unlock more machines, abilities, weapons, etc, and exploring the large map to obtain the resources to make what you need. There's a good variety of zones, and plenty of places to explore, from wealthy cities to creepy forests. Travel is interesting given you can shapeshift into many different forms, and horses can be ridden (and trained/improved).

You can obtain servants to help you gather resources as the game progresses, so you're spending more time fighting and exploring rather than having to farm materials.

Optimisation is good, and with all settings maxed playing at 4k/120Hz my rig (RTX 4090/7800X3D) was barely tested. I imagine players with older machines can expect decent performance given how well the game ran on my machine.

I did not purchase the DLC as it's strictly cosmetic, and there are so many options with the base game that I didn't feel the need. Although it was nice to know that sections of the game aren't gated behind DLC. I felt that this was a fair and responsible approach to DLC, and appreciate the devs' attitude with respect to this often problematic area.

Basically if you like this kind of game (beating bosses to progress, experimenting with combat, exploring, and base building), then you're likely to enjoy V Rising. The game looks great, plays great, and there's a lot to keep you busy. The whole package comes across as very polished.

I literally don't have a bad thing to say about the game, which is unusual, as I'm a pretty picky gamer and it doesn't take much to set me off. I'll definitely be checking out what Stunlock Studios come up with next.

Warning. If you want to play this game because you like Valheim and want a similar experience?
Forget this game.

Anyone trying to sell you that this is Valheim with Vampires is full of it.

It's a very good game, but one that mainly focuses on Combat, PvE and specially PvP. With a lot of crafting.

However, if you are edging to experience something similar to Valheim, you will be be disappointed.

- The Exploration aspect in V Rising is lacking. Yes the map is very big, but because it's not proceduraly generated, there just isn't this sense of exploration and discovery. The Top down aRPG view also hinders in this regard.

- The base building. Is a thing. But it's very basic. Don't get me wrong, you will be spending a LOT of time building and expanding your castle in V Rizing. But that's main to increase it's size, unlock new things and maybe decorate the rooms.  The game however offers very little creative freedom to create your own pieces of art in that regard. Your castle is essentially a set of tiles and walls, with added wallpapers and decoration. That's about the extend of it. So if you are interested in buidling amazing structures? Forget, this ain't the game for you.

This game is for those who want a survival game with solid combat, which offer both PvE and PvP (the later being the best experience I think). And while you can play it solo, it will feel tedious very fast, so it's a game that is best played with a group of friends. It also has a very solid crafting system and for an EA access game, it's honestly worth the 20 bucks.

But know what your buying. Don't be fooled by the review calling this "Valheim with Vampires" because that's definitely not the case.

Its a great game, Its great with friends on private server, just building the castle and doing all the bosses, ended up soloing the last bosses on brutal difficulty for a nice challenge. So many ways to play.

Though a very big con. Why do the servers need to be reset for the new content, if valheim can add it, im sure a game without random generation should have an easier time...

A lot of people are referring to this as "Vampheim" and it's a nice buzz word, but I don't think it adequately gets across the actual core of what this game is. 

Yes, you need to eat (feed) to survive
Yes, you craft and build
Yes, there are bosses to fight that give you increasing power gains as you beat them
Yes, those bosses are farmable

But

The combat is way better
The game has PvP as a core design element (but you still have the option to play on a PvE only server)
The building is NOT as good as in valheim, specifically it isn't as open and customizable. The buildings do LOOK very nice but that's because they remove a lot of the freedom from Valheim. This also removes a lot of the stress of building. 

Overall I think this game is incredible and it's the best "I am a Vampire" experience available in modern gaming, in my opinion.

Update: I want to address the large number of people who are complaining about the game "still" being in early access 5 months later, and lacking content updates.

Both of those are true statements, and if that alone is enough to deter you so be it. I won't bother trying to defend the studio or anything, I know they have a history. But the reason I'm still recommending the game is that you can easily get 200 hours or more out of this game IN IT'S CURRENT STATE, and it's $20 at full price (Yes I only have 121 hours currently, but I have almost 900 games in my steam library and I have a problem). Most of these negative reviews come from the free weekend and HAVE over 200 hours played, but they don't recommend it because "Devs Bad". 

My reviews are not based on some perceived place of morality, nor on some utopian ideal of how things "Should be". If you like Survival games, games with fluid combat, games with PvP, or just games that make you feel like a vampire then this will be some of the best $20 you ever spent.

I’m not writing this out of hatred for the game. I’m writing it because I genuinely cared about it, and this whole situation has been incredibly frustrating and disappointing.

A really fun, really great core concept held back slightly (for me) by some annoyances, most of which are just down to personal preference. 

The core gameplay loop is fun -- unlock technology, improve vampire, tackle boss to unlock technology/combat abilities, improve vampire, all whilst building up a proper gothic castle to live in -- but it can be a bit uneven. There have been a few points at which I've been bottlenecked overly-long by the difficulty of acquiring a single material (lookin at you, greater blood essences), or because the trajectory of improvements that propels you to new bosses has a significant gap in it (60-ish, a gear level that isn't comfortable for the new areas I have to venture into in order to continue progressing). 

I like the way they've done the combat a lot, in particular the way you can change your loadout on the fly. Combined with the blood types/potencies, there's a lot of room here to create fun builds. Some bosses have felt undertuned, some overtuned, but there are some great fights -- and a couple that felt sorta cheap. Increasingly as I level I find myself getting annoyed by the approach to increasing the difficulty: either 'overwhelming numbers of enemies' or 'roaming baddies in each zone of a level high enough that you absolutely cannot do anything about them other than run away until you've outleveled the zone.' 

I'm not a fan of that method of difficulty increase, I guess; I prefer a skill-surmountable kind (like a boss with a complex move-set). It's an approach that punishes solo play in particular, since numbers and especially tough enemies can both be tackled easily by groups...but a lot of the game's other choices suggest that, although it does offer a solo mode, it's really not meant to be played that way. 

This set-up leads to a lot of moments that feel senselessly punishing to me, or at best arbitrarily frustrating. You will want to collect prisoners with a high-potency blood of each type, and you will often watch helplessly as a bafflingly tanky longbow archer repeatedly sets all of her friends on fire and the high-% individual you spotted melts in puddles of fire you can do nothing about. You will go to a specific location to harvest something you absolutely need in great quantities in order to progress, and then find yourself chased away from it, losing an entire night of game-time, by wandering baddies you're literally not equipped to deal with -- and won't be until you've obtained those materials in those quantities. You'll have to come back the next evening...but maybe they'll still be there, and you won't get your materials then, either. Or maybe you'll get surprised by a skull-difficulty patrol (or two, or three) as you're fighting your way there, and have to turn back before you even get there.

For me, stuff like this doesn't make a game 'harder,' it just makes it sort of irritating/time-consuming/tedious in those areas. But as I've said, that's just me; you may feel differently about it. I think it would be less annoying if you could travel more reliably between points without having to dump your inventory, but I expect that's not on the table because the game is intended to be a PVP game, and they want to force people to be out on the map.

It obviously hasn't kept me from sinking 73 hours into the game, and that number will probably continue to climb until I hit the end of the content available now, so that's a pretty strong endorsement.

I hope they do something about items becoming unlootable whenever they fall down next to tent walls or other static objects, though. Lost like 3 books that way.

I've played this game for 26 hours in the past two days. 

[u][b]TL;DR; It's good.[/b][/u]

[b]A bit of background on how I am currently playing the game:[/b]

I am currently playing it on a solo-duo official PVP server. When you die you lose all the resources you had on you but not the gear, I understand that there's a full loot drop mode as well, maybe not available for solo-duo server, i've only seen that option for the 4 man group servers. PVE servers are also available for those not interested in PVP.

[b]Who am I?[/b]
I'm Alex and I love survival games. I have around 4.5k hours in Rust and have dabbled in Albion, Last Oasis, Valheim, Conan Exiles and Subnautica. If you like survival games, this review is for you.

[b]What kind of game is it?[/b]
A top down RPG survival game with building/raiding mechanics. You are a Vampire that grows in power by improving the gear you are wearing - there is no EXP bar and your level is dictated by your gear score. From what I've observed, gear score is not that important in PVP but is important in PVE.

In order to advance through the game you have to unlock knowledge either by getting books, random research (it's not as bad as it sounds) or tracking bosses, fighting them and then absorbing their powers.

[b]Character build variety:[/b]
There's plenty and since the game just came out there is currently no meta that I have observed.

Depending on the type of weapon you have (sword, axes, mace, spear, reaper, slashers/dual blades or crossbow) and the material the weapon is made out of (bone, copper, iron - and i don't know what comes next) you will have between 0 and 2 abilities that you can cast with it. Cooldowns are shared but you can cast ability 1 with one weapon, swap to another and cast ability 2.

As you defeat more bosses you will unlock vampiric abilities or spells. You can equip a type of dash, two spells and one ultimate at any given time. You can swap these out freely but you can't do so while in combat.

There are currently 5 schools of magic: Blood, Unholy, Illusion, Chaos and Frost. Each offer 5 unique spells, a type of dash and an ultimate ability.

Equipment doesn't seem to vary a lot, you can wear items on chest, hands, legs, feet, trinket and cloak. There's an extra slot for a cosmetic head item, I have yet to find head pieces that grant stats. The only place where you have some wiggle room in terms of build is your jewelry slot, there are items geared towards survival, sustain, damage and spell power.

In addition to this, there's blood. Each living mob on the map has a type: Creature, Rogue, Warrior, Brute, Scholar and Worker. Depending on the blood type and blood level (this is randomized per mob from 1 to 100% and the deeper you go into the map the more common it is to find higher blood levels), you will get between 1 and 5 different bonuses. You can factor this in to your build. As time goes by your blood level will go down and you will have to find a new target to feed on. You can also use this blood to heal - this makes you immobile and vulnerable to attacks.

[b]PVP:[/b]
It's phenomenal. Getting ganked is usually a death sentence but there are ways of avoiding combat while outnumbered. Later on you might be able to win 1v2 fights but at the start it's a bit hard.

You can't really heal while in combat, the amount of health you can fully heal goes down as you take damage and while in combat you are flagged and can't heal above that threshold.

Fighting feels very responsive and most spells need to be targeted and therefore can be dodged.

[b]PVE:[/b]
Awesome! Mobs don't seem to be re-skinned versions and the higher their level, the more abilities they have. You will be killing NPCs a lot and honestly, running into a village and slaughtering all the innocent civilians running around and screaming "VAMPIRE!" is very satisfying.

[b]Building:[/b]
You're fairly limited in creativity but there are a lot of cosmetic items that make up for the fact that you can't build vertically. Depending on what type of player you are (you know, RUST PTSD or PVE expert) you'll either build a "Fuck you, here's a door on each tile base" or "Look at my magnificent castle".

[b]Raiding:[/b]
To be honest, I have not yet found it rewarding. It's expensive and if you want someone out for good it will cost a lot of resources as each castle has a heart and to take over that heart you will have to pay a big amount of resources.

On official servers there's a raiding window in place, you can only raid in the afternoon (4pm to 10pm GMT).

[b]Wrapping things up.[/b]
Is it Valheim? No. Is it a Hack&Slash? Maybe. Is it Albion? No.

The game has a unique setting and for an Early Access title it's totally worth the money as there is plenty of content and tech to unlock.

One of my favorite games this year and one of the best survival games ever made. It cuts away all of the things that make survival games a tedious slog. Don't let the early access stamp fool you. This game is polished to a brilliant sheen. 

There is literally only 1 thing I can't stand about the game. The castle decay system desperately needs to be revamped. I completed all of the content the game has to offer a few months ago and now I still have to log in to feed the castle heart once a week. Which means I have to go farm enemies for blood and bring it back to the castle, feed the heart, then log off. If you don't the castle decays and you can be easily raided at any time by other players while you are offline.

Game is great, lots of content, you can be a rat and prank peasants with bowl cuts

It is a complete, finished game with a lot of things to do; if anyone tells you it's "abandoned," then they don't know what that word means, and they need to stop thinking of everything like a perpetual live service game

[h1]A survival RPG with its own characteristics and a true understanding of vampires[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]★ 8.5/10 — The vampire gameplay is well done, and the survival process is indeed time-consuming[/h2]

[b]⊕ BEST FOR:[/b] Players who like vampire themes, castle construction, top-down combat, cooperative survival, fixed maps, open-world PvP, and custom Private Games.

[b]⊖ NOT FOR:[/b] Players who are unwilling to collect repeatedly, prefer random maps and story-driven RPGs, want to freely advance the process, permanently retain the progress of the Official Servers, or are ready to play single-player with the default settings.

[b]▣ Media Benchmarks:[/b] Metacritic PC 83/100 · OpenCritic 83/100 · IGN 9/10 · PC Gamer 89/100.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]◆ Opening[/h2]

As of Update 1.1: Invaders of Oakveil, new areas, bosses, weapons, and main features have been added through free updates, and paid DLC only involves cosmetic packs and soundtrack content.

[h2]◆ Strengths[/h2]

[b]⊕ The identity of a vampire does affect how you play[/b]
The sun will burn in a few seconds, and you have to find shadows on the way during the day, but the shadows will move over time. The blood pool has been consumed, and the bonuses provided by different Blood Types are also different. Shapeshifting can help rush, sneak, and explore, and some special areas must also be entered by it. Silver, garlic, and human settlements have their own places to pay attention to.

You will choose to hunt at night and go back before dawn. You will also detour because of the sun, the enemies on the road, or the blood type you are looking for.

Production, research, production of equipment, arrangement of Servants, and detention of Prisoners reserved as blood sources are all carried out in their own Gothic castles. At first it was just a place to stay, but slowly a decent vampire palace could be built. The Advanced Game Settings of Private Games can also adjust resource output, crafting time, enemy strength, blood drain, sunlight, and death penalties.

[b]⊕ The combat is excellent in the survival game, and the fixed map also makes value[/b]
The combat uses a top-down angle, WASD movement, mouse aiming, and movement abilities (Veils), weapon skills, and spells. With another weapon, the basic attack, skill, and attack range will all change; the spell school and equipment also support different builds such as melee, ranged, summoning, control, and damage over time.

It is not as complicated as a dedicated action game, but the movement, combat feedback, and build options are already better than most survival games. Many V Bloods have their own moves, arena mechanics, and phase changes, and they need to be familiar with them before they can deal with them. Brutal will increase skills and change combat behavior, not just increase health and damage.

The factions, resources, enemies and patrol routes in each area are different, and different factions can be encountered in the wild to fight each other. You can take the opportunity to pick up a bargain, or you may bump into a patrol that can't be beaten at all when you are on your way. After you are familiar with the map, the fun of exploring comes more from your understanding of the environment: where is it dangerous, which way to transport materials, and where to find suitable prey. These experiences are useful in collecting, castle site selection, and PvP.

[h2]◆ Weaknesses[/h2]

[b]⊖ The upgrading of the production chain makes the upgrade feel fulfilling, and it is really abrasive[/b]
The problem is that the later, the more steps will be taken to collect, refine, transport, and make a string. Many early materials have to continue to be collected in the later stage, because they still have to be used for advanced materials.

Version 1.1 reduces some chores in the castle. The Treasury allows the crafting and construction to directly use the territory inventory, and the Redistribution Engine can transfer items between production facilities, but it is relatively late to get it.

Private Games can increase resource output and shorten crafting time, but the steps to take are still those. To play alone, you have to fight monsters, collect, ship goods, arrange production, and maintain the castle by yourself. Two or more people divide the labor, and the rhythm will be much better.

Room and flooring bonuses will also affect the layout. If you want to build a castle beautifully, you have to consider production efficiency.

[b]⊖ Although the growth route is very clear, there is less freshness when replaying[/b]
Following the Journal, you basically know what to do next: defeat the V Blood boss, get the unlocked content (V Blood Unlocks), get new equipment, Spell Points and recipes, and then go to the back area until the final boss. Weapons and skills can be selected, and some bosses can also be played in a different order, but many tools necessary to advance the process still have to defeat the designated boss to get them.

If you start another game, it will still be those areas, roads and resource points, and the growth route will be much the same. Compared with survival games with randomly generated maps, after the first round is played, the next round can bring a lot less freshness of exploration.

[b]⊖ The castle needs to be reopened for large-scale updates, and the built castle will inevitably make people reluctant[/b]
As of version 1.1, large-scale content updates have made changes to maps, units, and systems, and players have been asked to reopen the save. The old local saves, Private Games, and self-hosted servers can be left in the corresponding old version to continue playing, but they cannot be brought into the updated world. The Official Servers will be reset during large-scale updates, or they may be cleared in a fixed cycle, and the characters, resources, and castles cannot be left forever.

If you can save the blueprint or building layout, at least you don't have to build it from scratch every time. Of course, map changes and server balance must also be considered, and it will not be as simple as directly importing the old save.

[b]⊖ Even if you have to fight for PvP, you have to fight for who has time[/b]
If players want to fight for territory and find each other's castle, they must also consider whether their layout is convenient for production or more resistant to Castle Raiding.

However, in a server that opens castle raids and wipes regularly, the amount of resources, clan size, online time, progression speed, and raid hours will all affect the results. Organized clans can collect, produce, and guard their homes separately, and it is much harder for small teams and people who enter the service late.

It's really exciting when the competition is fierce, but if you can't follow the server's schedule and want to stay competitive, you may have to invest more time than expected.

[h2]◆ Conclusion[/h2]

From the first time I played it in 2024 to the present, what I admire most is that "V Rising" has added so many things and still retains its original characteristics.

If you can accept fixed maps, linear growth, and are willing to spend time collecting and operating, the vampire survival experience it provides is indeed worth a try.

On one hand, I love this game. The gameplay is awesome, I  got more than my money's worth. I would love to recommend it, but I also have a lot of really bad feelings about this game. This game is early access, so if they fix the crippling problems then I will change this.

Why did I quit? for the same reason I can't recommend the title. There are some easy solutions to my problem such as don't play on a castle raiding pvp server, don't play pvp at all, or just always be online. This doesn't work for me, because the PVP IS fun when it's fair, and the only endgame content this game has is, in fact, pvp and castle raiding. Unfortunately if you work or can't be online during pvp times, your castle will get destroyed 100 percent and everything you've worked to farm will be taken. You could say, "well you'll still have your gear or you'll still have your abilities." But when you've farmed for hours and hours to make a perfect, beautiful creation and everything is taken the second you arent online for the pvp window, it's pretty defeating.

If you aren't careful, people can use some of the really cool abilities to just enter your castle no matter what you do and destroy/take things. That can be prevented to a degree if you're careful, but never entirely. There are a large number of decorations/fences that you wouldn't want to use because this makes your base weaker, not that it matters a whole lot in the end. If you aren't online, no matter what you did to build up, castle raiding is the equivalent of punching a baby and stealing its candy. There is nothing you can do about it.

What makes this a little more sad is you can charm servants and use them to defend your base, but that is basically pointless anyways. The mechanic is really cool, but if you arent there, they are the equivalent of a mosquito regardless of how hard you worked to find the most powerful servants and put the best gear on them. It takes a LOT, and i do mean a TON of resources to gear your servants, but its pointless in the end. I even went so far as to make my castle look ugly and silly by building layer after layer of honey-combed walls and doors that were a nuisance to go in and out. I put traps down via unintented mechanics by summoning NPC minions into the main entry choke-points of my walls. Things I had to navigate around to get in and out and it was a pain. But in the end it didn't matter.

If you piss someone off for any reason and they come from a better clan and have more free time than you, the first time you aren't on for the ENTIRE infinitely long pvp window, you've lost everything you made. There is an exception, a dinky lockbox that can contain a few items, but it is nowhere near enough to replace everything you lost and all the time you spent. You may be thinking, "ok, ill just wait until the next pvp window and destroy the guy that took me out and take everything back." Well, unfortunately, if they are online, you won't win.

There is only incentive to raid castles when another player is offline. Basically there is no end-game pvp. PVP is the end-game, so the loop is simply wait until person A is offline, walk into base with a very cheap golem, loot everything, walk away. So basically everything you work for will be taken by someone with infinite time. The first time this happened to me and everything was taken, I thought, "ill jump servers and start over. it'll be fun!" Well I did that, I was careful not to upset anyone via PVP, and it didn't matter. Eventually someone is going to want to get you. You make a big castle, you build it up, people with endless time will take and destroy everything the second you're offline.

This could be fixed if servants were powerful enough that the enemy actually had to contend with them. Or if you could set traps. Hell if the enemy couldnt just go bat-form and see inside your entire castle no matter what you did so they can plan an attack, that would help loads! Or if they couldnt go bat form and just drop into the cliff of your castle, walk in, and take stuff/scout/kill your npcs.

My advice is to wait until they make it so you can't raid castles with the castle host offline, or implement some sort of insurance system, or some paid defense system, or the ability to set traps. Another needed fix is that the enemy cant just know where your castle is the first time they go bat form, or drop anywhere near your castle, or see inside your entire base just by flying by with your name highlighted so they can instantly scout you out.

They can literally sit in bat form next to your castle, wait until you go offline because it shows them that you've gone offline, and then destroy and take everything from you. You cant stop them. Or if they had some actual endgame other than pvp, but the game was build around pvp as the end-game.

I played 228 hours, but am still recommending "No".

The good parts: it's a fun game, you collect all the mats, build your gear and kill all the bosses. The standard crafting game loop. The combat is good and diverse. The graphics and sounds are great, the action smooth.

The bad parts.

Most of all, the terribly forced multiplayer. This is one of those games where if you don't play all the time, you loose. Meaning, people will destroy your base when you are offline and that's that. You lost now, you won't be able to build up again.

Now, I was playing on a PvE server, so this doesn't happen. However, what happens when you don't play for a few days because, I don't know, maybe you have a life? Or playing some other game? Well guess what. All your progress is gone. Your mats, your end-game power pilars, your 100% scholar blood prisoner, your gold bars, your perfect castle (s), your fully geared power level 700+ servants. All you have is your gear, who's durability won't last you long enough to build all the way up to having access to the mats and crafting stations required to repair them.

There is no single-player mode, because all the things you have to wait for (we're talking 2-24 hours of wait times for missions and high level crafting) require the game to run for time to pass. The developers didn't think to just check the system clock. Because, you know, PvP! You can run a private server with adjusted settings which helps enough but it is a bit of a hassle with scripts and config files.

The sun mechanic is interesting at first (you're a vampire so the sun kills you), but it get's old quick. There is no real challenge here to overcome. If you plan to fight some boss out in the open, you're forced to wait until dusk (a boss fight typically takes around half the night in game time). So the sun mechanic is just a waste of time.

When you're just starting, you can choose an official server or a non-official. On official servers, you'll find it real hard to create a base or even get around in the world, because every buildable area in the starting zone is completely blocked off by idiots showing off their max rank castles. On unofficial servers, you might suddenly find that they went offline and you lost your character and castle,

For a multiplayer game, the multiplayer aspect is pretty shitty. First of all, performance is bad. It's starts lagging like mad even with one other player near. Secondly, the social aspect is bad. Chatting while doing combat or other things is clumsy because of how the key binds work. At the very least, they should allow easy toggle between global and local and have escape cancel the chat. You cannot make friends. You cannot communicate when people are offline, there's no way to send an email or anything.

There's no interesting interaction between the structures people build and the environment, it's all just max 2 castles per person.

The game offers a load of decoration options for your castles, you can make beautiful interiors, gardens etc but guess what? Nobody will ever see them, because everyone seems to simply but a big wall around their castles. So now every castle looks the same. Just a big wall blocking off what would be an interesting bit of scenery in the map.

If you still plan to play this game, here's my advise: pick an official server. Build your castle as close to the next zone as possible. Get servants as soon as possible to farm mats for you. And keep playing every day until you finished the game, then delete it and move on.

Big takeaway is that if you're looking for a singleplayer experience, avoid this game.

This game is SPECIFICALLY designed to be a co-op PVE or PVP experience.

Thematically, the game is about being a supervillain vampire who is gaining power after the vampires return from hibernation.

Mechanically, the game is really about exploration and unlocking the next set of gear and buildings via relatively well-done boss fights. The skills are well done because they all scale with your overall power level, making even the starting skills useful later in the game, and you definitely have to switch out active skills depending on what boss you are fighting.

The big catch is that if you're stuck on a boss, progression is often very hard because the next tier of equipment is locked behind the rewards for beating that boss. I haven't gotten permanently stuck on a boss yet, but I can see it happening.

You don't really get permanent rewards like XP from fighting enemies that don't give you worthwhile rewards - there's no combat grinding in this game (but there is a lot of resource grinding). I like this, however, as it really rewards stealth and picking your battles. There's no reason to fight if you don't get something from it. In addition, in-combat healing is really limited. Your level is entirely based off of your gear which is directly based off of what bosses you have fought.

I wish the game had a lot more social elements and a real society to deal with. Vampires in fiction are able to disguise themselves and seduce or corrupt the living, and that would be really exciting and fun to do. I think I'm about 40% of the way through the current content and there's not a shred of that to be seen yet. Disappointing in that regard.

EDIT: Turns out one of the bosses gives you a human disguise which is fun to sneak around in, so I was wrong on this one. I literally wrote this review right before I got to that content. It's just a disguise, though, there's still not a lot of "social" aspects of the game - it's pretty much entirely a combat game.

The basebuilding is fairly fun and really lets you make your spooky vampire castle.

We built a new location so we could make the siege golem and the castle keys so we could destroy that person's walls and get back to our own base. After fighting the other team, we successfully breached the castle after breaking through countless 1x1 rooms set up to block us from the heart. We accessed the heart and were told that hostile actions may only be taken against hearts in decay. That meant that we had to squat on their base and protect it from them for a week before it would go into decay. There were keys made specifically to destroy or take over someone's base, so why make those items obsolete on official servers?
